German media outlets have reported, citing western intelligence agency assessments, that such a satellite could be launched within 60 days and would be operational shortly afterwards.
Here we look at the implications of a nuclear weapon being detonated in space.
What is the report saying?
A report by the German broadcasters NDR and WDR and the newspaper Süddeutsche Zeitung said western intelligence services, including Germany’s Bundesnachrichtendienst (BND) intelligence service and armed forces, had exchanged information showing that a nuclear-enabled satellite, named Sputnik-S, was assembled several years ago and is stationed in the Moscow region. It could be launched this year. A German government spokesperson said it was taking the intelligence reports “very seriously”.
What impact could a nuclear device have if exploded in orbit?
In space, where there is no atmosphere, there is no mushroom cloud. Instead, the energy from a nuclear explosion is released as radiation. A detonation would be particularly damaging in low Earth orbit, or up to 1,200 miles above Earth, where most satellites operate.
Jonathan McDowell, an astrophysicist and honorary professor at the Durham University Space Research Centre in the UK, said the main effects were twofold: everything within line of sight of the detonation could be zapped by X-rays and other forms of radiation which could knock out or damage satellites within thousands of miles; secondly, radiation particles could be emitted into the lower atmosphere and form a new “Van Allen belt”, the term for two belts of radiation that circle the Earth and shield it from the impact of solar storms.
It would be a replay of an event in 1962 when the US detonated a thermonuclear bomb 250 miles above Earth’s surface – in low Earth orbit – in an event called Starfish Prime. There were many fewer satellites then but it shortened the life of two craft: the Telstar 1 and Ariel-1 satellites.
“Starfish caused severe radiation over a period of months to at least half the satellites then working on orbit, which was not very many at that point,” said McDowell.
Keith Ryden, a professor of space engineering at the University of Surrey in the UK, said low Earth orbit satellites were vulnerable to bursts of radiation.
“Since natural levels of radiation are relatively low in this region, satellites located there are not designed for high radiation levels so they would be vulnerable to unexpected increases,” he says.
What is the most damaging area of orbit for this to happen in?
There are about 17,000 satellites in lower Earth orbit, including satellites important to weather forecasting, climate monitoring and the military as well as Elon Musk’s network of satellites that form the Starlink broadband network. The latter is crucial to assisting Ukraine’s efforts in repelling the invasion of Russia.
The International Space Station, in which Russia is a partner, is also in low Earth orbit. Musk’s proposed constellation of space datacentres would operate there as well.
Satellites handling TV broadcast, GPS and other communications are in higher orbits that are less easy for a nuclear weapon to affect.
How long would it take to recover activity in the affected area of orbit?
McDowell said the artificial Van Allen belt caused by Starfish Prime was around for five years.
“There will be immediate impacts from a detonation but there are lasting environmental effects that will damage satellites in the longer run. It could take several years, up to a decade, for the trapped particles to diffuse out of the radiation belt,” he said.
Ryden added: “Just as important, the space industry would not have the capacity to rebuild and launch the required number of spacecraft in a short time.”
Would activity on Earth be immediately affected by an explosion?
Hundreds of miles below the Starfish Prime explosion, streetlights in Hawaii were knocked out, burglar alarms were set off in the area, and phone calls were disrupted.
“There might be an impact on computers and electronic systems in the region of earth where the explosion is visible,” said McDowell.
Ryden added that Starfish and other nuclear tests took place over sparsely populated areas so the location of the detonation was key.
“It does depend a lot on where the detonation happens,” he said.
Starfish Prime also created stunning aurora effects as the sky was lit up in shades of green, yellow, red and, according to one report, “tremendous white rainbows”.
“There would be huge auroral effects. It would not be a subtle thing. It’s hard to be subtle with nukes,” said McDowell.
Is Russia likely to detonate a nuclear warhead in space?
A European security official told the Guardian that they were doubtful that Russia would detonate a nuclear device in space. They said it could cause significant damage to western economies, but that it stood to significantly harm Russia as well. Such an explosion would be hard to control and would probably damage Russia’s own satellites, as well as, potentially, China’s. “It would be shooting themselves in the leg,” they said.
They pointed at Russia’s nuclear blackmail earlier in its war in Ukraine, including when Russia put its nuclear forces on high alert in 2022, followed by movements of troops and weapons. “They were bluffing then – and this looks like a bluff now,” said the official. McDowell said he was sceptical about Russia detonating a nuclear weapon in space, because it was “such a stupid idea” to commit what would be viewed as an act of war.
digest_he:
גופי תקשורת בגרמניה דיווחו, בהתבסס על הערכות של סוכנויות מודיעין מערביות, כי רוסיה הכינה לוויין בעל יכולת גרעינית בשם ספוטניק-S, אשר עשוי להיות משוגר לחלל כבר השנה. על פי המומחים, פיצוץ של נשק גרעיני במסלול לוויני נמוך לא ייצר פטריית עשן אלא ישחרר קרינה רבה, שתפגע קשות בלוויינים ותייצר חגורת קרינה מלאכותית דמויית חגורות ואן אלן.

אירוע דמה התרחש בשנת 1962 כאשר ארצות הברית ביצעה ניסוי גרעיני בגובה של 250 מייל מעל פני כדור הארץ, שקיצר את חייהם של לוויינים באותה תקופה. כיום ישנם אלפי לוויינים במסלול נמוך, כולל מערכות תקשורת ותשתיות קריטיות, העשויים להיפגע קשות. עם זאת, גורמי ביטחון אירופיים מטילים ספק בכך שמוסקבה תבצע מהלך שכזה, שכן הוא עלול לגרום נזק משמעותי גם ללוויינים של רוסיה עצמה ולפגוע בכלכלה העולמית.
